t: Carla Simulator: What CARLA Is: A City for Autonomy
title: Carla Simulator: What CARLA Is: A City for Autonomy
description: CARLA is an open-source driving simulator built on Unreal Engine: detailed urban maps with buildings, traffic lights, pedestrians, and weather, plus a Python API that spawns vehicles, attaches sensors, and steps the world. Researchers train and test perception, planning, and end-to-end driving policies in scenarios that would be dangerous or tedious on real streets. It is the standard benchmark environment for autonomous-driving papers — if a driving algorithm was published, it probably drove in CARLA.
key_facts: Python API for vehicles and sensors

t: Carla Simulator: Maps and Towns: The Urban Catalog
title: Carla Simulator: Maps and Towns: The Urban Catalog
description: CARLA ships a catalog of towns — from small rural loops to dense urban grids — each with road networks, intersections, traffic lights, and props. Maps are the test corpus: a planner validated on one town is a rumor; validated across the catalog, it is evidence. Custom maps can be built in RoadRunner or Unreal. The discipline is map diversity — the failure modes hide in the town you did not test.

t: Carla Simulator: Sensors: Configuring the Vehicle's Eyes
title: Carla Simulator: Sensors: Configuring the Vehicle's Eyes
description: CARLA sensors are configured like real hardware: lidar with channels, points-per-second, and noise; cameras with resolution, FOV, and lens effects; radar, GNSS with error models, IMU with drift. The Python API attaches them at vehicle-relative transforms and streams data each tick. Sensor configuration is experimental design — the suite you test with should bracket the hardware you will deploy on, from optimistic to pessimistic.

t: Carla Simulator: Traffic Manager and Pedestrians
title: Carla Simulator: Traffic Manager and Pedestrians
description: Empty streets teach nothing, so CARLA's Traffic Manager drives background vehicles with configurable aggression, and pedestrians wander sidewalks and crosswalks. Scenario Runner scripts the critical moments — the jaywalker, the cut-in, the red-light runner. The realism debate never ends, but the practice is settled: test against traffic that misbehaves, because real traffic does.

t: Carla Simulator: Your First Drive: Spawning and Waypoints
title: Carla Simulator: Your First Drive: Spawning and Waypoints
description: The hello-world: connect the Python client, spawn a vehicle at a waypoint, attach a camera, and drive it along waypoints while saving images. Ten lines of API, and you have a dataset generator. From there: add lidar, add traffic, record rosbags. Every CARLA project starts here, and the engineers who master the API's transform math (vehicle-relative vs world coordinates) master the sim.

t: Carla Simulator: The Python API: Control Patterns
title: Carla Simulator: The Python API: Control Patterns
description: CARLA's Python API is the steering wheel: synchronous vs asynchronous mode (fixed time-step for determinism), batch commands for spawning hundreds of actors efficiently, and the world tick as the heartbeat. The patterns that scale are batch spawning, sensor listen callbacks that only copy what you need, and deterministic fixed-step runs for reproducible experiments. API fluency — transforms, waypoints, blueprints — is CARLA fluency.

t: Carla Simulator: Weather and Time of Day
title: Carla Simulator: Weather and Time of Day
description: CARLA's weather system — sun angle, cloudiness, precipitation, fog, wetness — changes what the sensors see: rain streaks the camera, wet roads reflect lidar differently, fog kills range. Robustness testing sweeps these parameters because the field will. A perception stack that only trained at noon in clear skies is a fair-weather stack, and fair-weather stacks fail at dusk in rain.

t: Carla Simulator: Scenario Runner: Scripting the Hard Cases
title: Carla Simulator: Scenario Runner: Scripting the Hard Cases
description: Scenario Runner is CARLA's test harness: XML-described scenarios (cut-ins, jaywalkers, blocked lanes) executed against the driving stack with pass/fail criteria — collision, lane invasion, route completion, infractions. The scenario catalog is the regression suite for driving: every stack change replays the hard cases. Writing new scenarios from field incidents is the maturity marker.

t: Carla Simulator: Defensive Uses: Safe Validation of Driving Stacks
title: Carla Simulator: Defensive Uses: Safe Validation of Driving Stacks
description: CARLA's defensive value is validation without victims: emergency braking, obstacle avoidance, and degraded-sensor behavior can be tested against thousands of scenarios no test track could stage. For uncrewed ground vehicles in controlled areas — logistics yards, campuses, perimeters — CARLA-style validation is how the safety case gets its evidence. The sim does not replace the track; it earns the right to go to the track.

t: Carla Simulator: Perception Training: Synthetic Datasets
title: Carla Simulator: Perception Training: Synthetic Datasets
description: CARLA generates labeled datasets for free: every frame comes with segmentation, depth, and bounding boxes from the ground truth. Teams pre-train perception on synthetic data, then fine-tune on real — or use sim to cover the long tail (rare weather, rare obstacles) the real dataset lacks. The domain gap is real but manageable: sim-to-real transfer works when the sim's noise and diversity are honest.

t: Carla Simulator: Debugging: Why Did It Crash (Virtually)
title: Carla Simulator: Debugging: Why Did It Crash (Virtually)
description: CARLA debugging is replay debugging: the recorder logs every actor's trajectory, so a crash replays exactly — watch the pedestrian's path, the planner's decision, the sensor frame that mattered. The common causes are planner timeouts (sim tick vs wall clock), sensor misconfiguration, and scenario seeds. The discipline is deterministic replay: same seed, same crash, every time, until the fix.
key_facts: Decision traces show the planner's reasoning

t: Carla Simulator: Performance: Running CARLA at Scale
title: Carla Simulator: Performance: Running CARLA at Scale
description: CARLA is hungry — Unreal rendering plus sensor simulation wants real GPUs. The scaling patterns are headless servers with GPU, sensor load budgeting (lidar points-per-second is the big knob), and fixed time-steps for determinism. Multi-client setups run many vehicles against one server. The economics are still kind: a GPU server farm costs less than one instrumented test vehicle.

t: Carla Simulator: Testing: Benchmarks and Leaderboards
title: Carla Simulator: Testing: Benchmarks and Leaderboards
description: CARLA's benchmarks (the original benchmark, then the Leaderboard) standardized driving evaluation: routes with scenarios, infraction penalties, completion scores. Leaderboards drove the field forward — and taught its limits, as teams overfit to the benchmark's quirks. The mature practice is private held-out scenarios plus the public benchmark: public for comparison, private for truth.
key_facts: Private matrix is the exam, not homework

t: Carla Simulator: Real-World Pattern: Yard Autonomy Validation
title: Carla Simulator: Real-World Pattern: Yard Autonomy Validation
description: A complete pattern: an uncrewed yard truck validated in CARLA-style sim — dock approaches, pedestrian zones, night rain — across the ordeal matrix, then graduated to the closed yard with a safety driver, then to supervised autonomy. Each stage's evidence gates the next. The sim did not drive the truck; it proved the truck deserved to drive.
